associationClusters.association: China moved from severe production interruption toward restart while many overseas economies were entering shutdowns. The investment question is not broad recovery but which China-based producers gained relative capacity availability or import-substitution bargaining power.
expressionArchetypes: export manufacturers with functioning Chinese capacity
automation suppliers benefiting from resilience/capacity reconfiguration

associationClusters.association: Dry-bulk recovery broadened into container-volume recovery and then a strong Asian export cycle. Read together, these stories imply rising utilization and a possible profit-pool transfer across carriers, ports, container equipment and export logistics before a single headline necessarily names the whole chain.
Huawei restrictions, China-India supply-chain friction and record chip imports/stockpiling point to a broader resilience/localization response rather than a single-company story.
expressionArchetypes: equipment/material suppliers with verified substitution demand

associationClusters.association: Consumer-facing digital platforms recovered while manufacturing activity accelerated. The second-order question is which A-share logistics, automation, payment, packaging or consumer-supply-chain businesses gained from the mix shift, not simply whether internet platforms recovered.

Weak aviation fuel demand and crude inventory accumulation coexisted with refinery expansion, while by December industrial/electricity demand was strong enough to trigger local power restrictions. This suggests major product-level and regional divergence inside 'energy', requiring winner/loser mapping rather than a single bullish commodity view.
expressionArchetypes: industrial users exposed to power scarcity

associationClusters.association: Domestic easing followed by unusually strong demand for Chinese dollar debt suggests improving financing conditions. This is a market-structure signal; only companies whose refinancing cost or balance-sheet constraint changes materially should proceed to company underwriting.
expressionArchetypes: brokers/financial intermediaries only with direct earnings bridge

associationClusters.association: National procurement was not merely a healthcare headline: it represented a sharp price and market-share reset. The opportunity search should separate generic producers that gain volume/share from originators or high-price incumbents that lose economics, then test whether lower prices still leave acceptable margins.
expressionArchetypes: incumbents exposed to severe price compression

associationClusters.association: Developer leverage constraints plus visible supplier dependence imply a balance-sheet and customer-concentration regime shift. Search for low-leverage developers and suppliers with diversified customers; separately mark highly concentrated suppliers as risk cases.

Foreign asset-management entry plus strong demand for Chinese securities suggests structural expansion in domestic wealth/asset-management infrastructure. The listed-company opportunity requires a direct fee-income, distribution or custody bridge rather than generic financial beta.

Some exporters were simultaneously regaining foreign demand and building domestic channels. A company able to pivot across channels may have lower demand risk and better capacity utilization than a pure exporter.
expressionArchetypes: consumer manufacturers with flexible channel mix

associationClusters.association: Release/transfer of a very large strategic metal stockpile can alter apparent scarcity for years. Treat this first as a negative/relative supply signal and search for metals where inventory disposition changes pricing power or downstream input costs.
expressionArchetypes: downstream users benefiting from cheaper inputs
